items.stem: What is the main advantage of just-in-time privileged access over standing admin rights?

options.text: Privileges exist only when needed, shrinking the window of exposure
options.rationale: Correct: time-bound access reduces the attack window.

options.text: It removes the need to authenticate administrators
It makes all accounts permanent administrators
options.rationale: That is the opposite of JIT.

options.text: It eliminates the need for any auditing

items.explanation: Correct: time-bound access reduces the attack window.

items.stem: Which TWO practices strengthen privileged credential management? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Vault privileged passwords and rotate them automatically
options.rationale: Correct: vaulting plus rotation limits reuse and exposure.

options.text: Retrieve secrets from a vault instead of hard-coding them
options.rationale: Correct: removing hard-coded secrets reduces leakage risk.

options.text: Share one admin password across the whole team
options.rationale: Shared passwords destroy accountability and are easily leaked.

options.text: Store credentials in a plaintext spreadsheet
options.rationale: Plaintext storage is a major exposure.

items.stem: Why record privileged sessions even for trusted staff?

options.text: To provide accountability and evidence of who did what
options.rationale: Correct: recording supports audit, investigation and deterrence.

options.text: Because trusted staff never make mistakes
options.rationale: Trusted staff still err; recording helps investigate.
The goal is accountability, not slowing work.
Recording complements, not replaces, access controls.

items.explanation: Correct: recording supports audit, investigation and deterrence.
